Baltimore Ballot explains Baltimore City ballot decisions. Everett Anderson makes and maintains the site. It is independent of city government and political campaigns.

## What It Covers

The site covers Baltimore City Questions A–H from the 2024 ballot and Questions A–I from the 2026 ballot. Statewide questions and candidate directories are outside the current scope.

The guides explain the choices without telling readers how to vote. They bring together plain-language explanations, official wording, measure types, topics, ballot origins, and sourced results.

## Sources And Standards {#editorial-standards}

Factual explanations and results link to the records behind them, and official wording is preserved as published. Ballot origin identifies the formal route to the ballot, not an endorsement.

## Understanding Results

Unofficial and Certified describe the status of the source. Neither label means a measure has been implemented. The 2024 City records use final official returns and are recorded as Certified; the 2026 records are an Unofficial snapshot.

Checked dates identify when a source was reviewed, not when results were certified. When counts are supplied, displayed vote shares use For plus Against votes, not all ballots. Missing counts are not zero. Passage does not establish bond issuance, spending, or completed projects.

## Corrections

Results and source records are maintained manually; they are not a live election feed. If a substantive mistake is corrected, the affected page will say what changed and when.
